_README: Copy the `permissions` block below into the .claude/settings.json of a CONSUMING repo.
This is the permissions half of the merge gate, and it needs no hook at all.
Why permissions-only, and not a PreToolUse hook. Measured 2026-08-30: an external
read-only consumer's driver refuses to run against a repository that ships its own
PreToolUse hook, and it raises HookRefusal with no override flag, so a repo that
installs one becomes undirectable by the runner. A deny and ask list costs nothing in
that direction: it is data the client already evaluates, not a second program
competing for the same slot.
deny is the destructive-git list this workflow's own .claude/settings.json carries. It
exists because a per-machine .claude/settings.local.json commonly accumulates a broad
allow entry such as Bash(git *), which pre-approves the destructive spellings along with
the read-only majority. Deny is evaluated before allow, so this narrows that window
without the local file having to be edited.
ask turns merge and marking a draft ready for review into a confirmation rather than a
refusal. Those two acts reach reviewers and the base branch, an audience that is not
bounded. git push is deliberately not in ask: a push to a task branch reaches a bounded
audience, and pr-package --apply pushes and opens the draft PR on its own invocation with
no second prompt (ADR-0185, ADR-0200). Drop the ask block if a human already merges every
PR by hand, or if you drive this repo with a runner that cannot answer a prompt: an
unanswerable ask is a hang, not a gate.
Two limitations, stated so the list is not mistaken for a guarantee. Matching is by
prefix, so a chained invocation (cmd && git reset --hard), an alias, or a refspec-force
spelling (git push origin +main) is not caught. And it bounds the agent's tool calls,
not the terminal: anything typed directly in a shell is unaffected. One layer, not the
control. See docs/HOOKS.md for the same caveats in prose.
